faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see horizontal or vertical lines in my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Perform a nozzle check from the printer's control panel or the Epson printer driver, then do one of the following:
If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: Which type of ink does my product use?
faqs.answer: The printer uses aqueous pigmented ink.

faqs.question: How many black ink cartridges can I install in my product at one time?
faqs.answer: The printer uses two black ink cartridges: Photo Black (PK) and Matte Black (MK).

faqs.question: Does my product use a maintenance box?
faqs.answer: Yes, it uses two maintenance boxes, part number T6193000.

faqs.question: Does my product use the same maintenance box as other Epson large format products?
faqs.answer: Yes, it uses the same maintenance box as the Epson T-Series printers, part number T6193000.

faqs.question: What media thickness will my product accept?

The printer accepts the following thickness.
Roll paper
: 0.003 to 0.02 inches (0.08 to 0.5 mm)
Cut sheet paper
: 0.003 to 0.06 inches (0.08 to 1.5 mm)

faqs.question: I see inconsistent color results when I print step and repeat images across a sheet of media. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Create a Custom Paper setting for your media by adjusting the following settings:
Paper Feed Adjustment
Head Alignment
Paper Thickness
To adjust these settings, do the following:
Clean the print head if necessary. See these
instructions
.
Load the media type you want to use in the printer.
Press the
Menu
button, select
Paper
, and then press
OK
.
Select
Custom Paper Setting
, and then press
OK
. Press the up or down arrow button to select a paper configuration number from 1 to 10, and then press
OK
.
Select
Select Reference Paper
and select the media type you loaded in the printer.
Note:
We recommend choosing a paper that closely matches the white point and thickness of the paper you are using. For proofing, we recommend you use Epson Proofing Paper White Semimatte.
Select
Platen Gap
, select a Platen Gap setting.
Select
Paper Thickness
, and then press
OK
. You need to convert your paper thickness setting from mils to millimeters to know which setting to select.
Select
Paper Feed Adjust
>
Block Pattern
and then press
OK
.
A pattern similar to the one below prints.
Examine the pattern and select the number of the pattern with the least separation (a white line in the middle) or overlap (a dark line in the middle).
A second pattern similar to the one below prints. Select the number of the pattern with the lightest density.
Adjust the following settings, if necessary:
Paper Suction
: Adjust the paper suction level when you print on thin media (under 12 pounds [5.4 kg]), such as drafting paper or back light film.
Roll Paper Back Tension
: Adjust the tension for cloth, thin paper, or paper that wrinkles during printing.
Remove Skew
: Enable paper skew reduction.
Setting Name
: Enter a name for the custom paper setting.
Press the
Menu
button, select
Maintenance
>
Head Alignment
>
Auto (Bi-D)
, and then press
OK
.
Note:
If you plan to create dot proofs, perform the Auto method and verify it with the Manual method.
Note:
Do not open the front cover or turn off the printer during the alignment process.

faqs.question: Does my product come with a built-in cutter?
faqs.answer: Yes, the printer comes with a built-in cutter with a user replaceable blade.

faqs.question: Can I use the Paper Feed Stabilizer setting with any media type?
faqs.answer:
No, it will work with most Epson media. It works with media that has a texture on the back.
Note:
The function is not available for transparent or colored media types.

faqs.question: Can the hard drive be moved to another printer to re-print jobs?
faqs.answer: No, the print jobs cannot be printed on another printer. If you insert the hard drive into another printer, it will prompt you to re-format the hard drive or ignore it.

faqs.question: Is an optional automatic take-up reel available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes, an optional automatic take-up reel is available for purchase (part number C12C932201).

faqs.question: What is the minimum cut sheet paper size my product will accept?
faqs.answer: The minimum cut sheet paper size is A4 (8.3 x 11.7 inches [210 x 297 mm]).

faqs.question: How many print heads does my product have?
faqs.answer: The printer has one advanced PrecisionCore MicroTFP Piezo-based print head.

faqs.question: What is the size of the print head?
faqs.answer: The printer has an advanced PrecisionCore MicroTFP Piezo-based print head that is 2.64 inches wide.

faqs.question: What is the maximum supported media width?
faqs.answer: The maximum supported media width is 44 inches (1118 mm) for roll paper, cut sheet paper and poster board.

faqs.question: How many nozzles does the print head have?
faqs.answer: The print head has 8000 nozzles arranged in 20 lines with 400 nozzles per color.

faqs.question: What is Nozzle Verification Technology?
faqs.answer: It is a new technology the printer uses to verify a nozzle printed correctly.

faqs.question: Which type of print head does my product use?
faqs.answer: The printer uses an advanced PrecisionCore MicroTFP Piezo-based print head.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
